title: Rounding and Estimation: Decimals, Money and Checking Answers
seo_title: Year 7 Rounding and Estimation Worksheets: Decimal Places, Rounding Money and Estimating (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: round decimals to a given accuracy appropriate to the context and use appropriate rounding and estimation to check the reasonableness of solutions
meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on rounding and estimation for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7N05): decimal places, rounding money to the nearest cent and 5c, estimating calculations and checking answers. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Look at the next digit: 5 or more, round up.
key_sub: Estimate by rounding each number to its leading digit: 38.7 × 21.4 ≈ 40 × 20 = 800.
body_html:
How it works

To round, find the last digit you keep, then look at the next digit: 5 or more, round up; 4 or less, keep it.

Choose the accuracy that suits the situation: money to the nearest cent, cash to the nearest 5c (Australia has no 1c or 2c coins), a height to the nearest centimetre. Sometimes the situation decides: 130 people need 3 buses of 50, not 2.6.

To estimate, round each number to its leading digit, then calculate. Use the estimate to check a calculator answer.

Example

Round 3.8462 to 2 decimal places.

Keep 3.84. The next digit is 6, so round up.

Answer: 3.85

Example

A cash total is $12.37. What is paid?

7c rounds to 5c.

Answer: $12.35

Example

Estimate 38.7 × 21.4.

38.7 ≈ 40 and 21.4 ≈ 20.

40 × 20 = 800.

Answer: 800

Common mistakes

  • Cutting off digits instead of rounding: 2.36 to 1 d.p. is 2.4, not 2.3.
  • Rounding to the wrong place: check which column you keep before you look at the next digit.
  • Leaving off a final zero: 9.97 to 1 d.p. is 10.0, not 10.
  • Rounding down when the situation needs rounding up, such as buses or boxes needed.

faq.q: How do I round to 2 decimal places?
faq.a: Keep two digits after the point and look at the third: 5 or more rounds up. 3.846 becomes 3.85.

faq.q: Why are cash prices rounded to 5c in Australia?
faq.a: There are no 1c or 2c coins, so cash totals are rounded to the nearest 5c. Card payments are not rounded.
To check that a calculator answer is reasonable. If 38.7 × 21.4 should be about 800, then 8281.8 must be wrong.

faq.q: Should I always round to the nearest whole number in word problems?
faq.a: No. If you need enough buses or boxes, round up. If only full boxes count, round down.

items.q: A shop total is $8.59. Australia has no 1c or 2c coins, so cash totals are rounded to the nearest 5c. How much do you pay in cash?
items.e: Totals ending in 1c or 2c round down to 0c; 3c, 4c, 6c and 7c round to 5c; 8c and 9c round up. So $8.59 becomes $8.60.

items.q: Estimate the cost of 19 movie tickets at $21.95 each.
Estimate the cost of 32 school jumpers at $38.50 each.
Estimate the cost of 48 exercise books at $2.95 each.

Estimate the cost of 9 pool passes at $7.10 each.
Isla works out 38.7 × 21.4 on a calculator and gets 8281.8. Use an estimate to decide if this is reasonable.
items.e: 38.7 × 21.4 ≈ 40 × 20 = 800, so 8281.8 is about 10 times too big. (The answer is 828.18.)

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 0.48 × 61?
Which is the best estimate for 612 ÷ 2.9?
A car uses 7.9 L of fuel per 100 km. Estimate the fuel used on a 395 km trip.
items.e: 395 km ≈ 400 km = 4 lots of 100 km, and 7.9 ≈ 8, so about 4 × 8 = 32 L.

items.q: Estimate the area of a bedroom 4.85 m by 3.12 m.
Which accuracy makes most sense for the price of petrol per litre in dollars?
c: To the nearest tenth of a cent, such as $1.879
items.e: Petrol prices are shown in cents and tenths of a cent, so to the nearest tenth of a cent.

items.q: Which is the most sensible way to give a person's height?
c: To the nearest metre, such as 2 m
To 5 decimal places of a metre
To the nearest centimetre, such as 1.62 m
To the nearest millimetre of a millimetre
items.e: Heights are usually given to the nearest centimetre.

items.q: Round 9.97 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 9.97 rounds up to 10.0. Keep the .0 to show 1 decimal place.

items.q: A recipe needs 0.375 kg of flour. Round this to the nearest tenth of a kilogram.
items.e: The digit after the 3 is 7, so round up: 0.4 kg.

items.q: Liam's calculator says 53 ÷ 7 = 7.571428571. What is this to 2 decimal places?
items.e: The digit after the 7 in the hundredths is 1, so round down: 7.57.

items.q: A cash total of $19.98 is rounded to the nearest 5c. What is paid?
items.e: 8c rounds up to 10c, so $19.98 becomes $20.

items.q: Estimate 6.1² + 49.3.
Mia estimates 297 × 51 as 300 × 50. Is her estimate more or less than the exact answer?
c: Less, because 51 was rounded down more than 297 was rounded up
items.e: 300 × 50 = 15 000 and 297 × 51 = 15 147, so the estimate is less.

items.q: Which calculation gives the best estimate of 4.92 × 19.6?
items.e: Round each number to its leading digit: 5 × 20 = 100.

items.q: A bottle holds 1.25 L. Round this to the nearest litre.
items.e: The digit after the 1 is 2, so round down: 1 L.
